name: Ares, Aphrodite, Harmonia, Eros, Hephaestus and Poseidon — the whole relation
description: Demodocus' song in whole sequence: the bed, the bonds, the distinct genealogies, generative difference, the capture apparatus stalled at its own limit, Poseidon's surety, and the relation after release.

scenes.name: The song, the bed, and the gods at the door
scenes.character: Demodocus takes the lyre among the Phaeacians; the tale turns to Ares and Aphrodite in Hephaestus's house.

text.title: The song, the bed, and the gods at the door
text.italic: The song demonstrates an exposure, a dispute, an undertaking and a release — payment is not narrated; no repaired marriage ends it.

text.body: Demodocus takes up his lyre among the Phaeacians; Odysseus has watched the dancers' feet. The song turns to Ares and Aphrodite, who met secretly in the house of Hephaestus. Helios saw the lovers and carried the news to the husband — and watched again, later, when the unseen work had closed.
Occurrences: Demodocus' lyre and the dancers' circle (#0 opening); Helios' first seeing and report (#0); the secret meeting in Hephaestus' house (#0).

scenes.name: Bonds beyond the gods' sight
scenes.character: Hephaestus forges bonds no one can break or loosen, arranges them around the bed, and pretends to leave for Lemnos.

text.title: δεσμοὶ τεχνήεντες — bonds as fine as a spider's web
text.italic: The craft demonstrates what technique can enclose: the bonds are beyond even the gods' sight, and the same hands will later undo them.

text.body: In pain and anger Hephaestus sets his anvil and makes bonds that can neither be broken nor loosened — around the bedposts, suspended from the beams, fine as a spider's web, beyond the gods' sight. He pretends to leave for Lemnos. Ares sees the husband gone, takes Aphrodite's hand, and the unseen work closes; only then do they know escape is impossible.

Occurrences: anvil and forge (#0); bedposts, beams, spider's-web bonds (#0); feigned departure to the Sintians of Lemnos (#0); Ares' own watch supplying the trap's occasion (#0, #3); Helios' second report (#0).

scenes.name: The children belong to their own tellings
scenes.character: Hesiod's Harmonia with Deimos and Phobos; Eros' separate genealogies — brought into the field without entering Demodocus' release scene.

entities.name: Harmonia's line — Cadmus, Ino, Semele, Agave, Autonoë, Polydorus

text.title: The children belong to their own tellings
text.italic: The distinct witnesses preserve their seams: no single family tree is forced, and no child is added to the release scene.

text.body: Hesiod's Theogony bears Deimos and Phobos — terror and fear — and Harmonia, whom Cadmus marries into a human line. Eros belongs among the primordial powers at 116–122 and accompanies Aphrodite's sea-birth; a separately reported lyric parentage (Simonides, in scholia) makes him child of Ares and Aphrodite. These tellings enter the field without joining Demodocus' scene: Harmonia the named child; Eros attraction and, in the variant, living desire.

Occurrences: Deimos and Phobos born of the same parentage (#1); Harmonia's marriage to Cadmus and descendants (#1); primordial Eros (#1); Aphrodite from the sea with Eros and Himeros (#1); Simonides' reported parentage (#1).

scenes.name: The difference that can meet — the bow that is also a lyre
scenes.character: Ares bears distinct being and refusal; Aphrodite attraction and joining; Harmonia the form sustained through their countertension.

entities.name: Harmonia — the form of their countertension
Eros — the desiring between (appointed filial variant)
bow and lyre — the backwards-turning fastening

text.kicker: #2 · Taylor's amplification; A13/C23–C25; Heraclitus B51; Q27 hamartia
text.title: The difference that can meet
text.italic: Harmonia figures the new form sustained through countertension — the parents keep contributing their powers inside what their meeting generates.

text.body: Ares carries distinct being, refusal, defence — the force by which a difference can stand. Aphrodite carries attraction, pleasure, the movement of joining. Each office is productive: a difference able to stand can enter a relation; attraction can make it generative. Harmonia figures the form sustained through their countertension; Eros, in the appointed filial variant, figures the desiring between. Deimos and

Phobos remain beside the family: differentiation can become hostility; joining can demand the other surrender its difference. Heraclitus B51: what differs agrees through a backwards-turning fastening, as bow and lyre. The bow forgets it is a lyre when tension collapses into a target — Q27's hamartia re-entry (human-amplified: yes for that exact quilt operation).

scenes.name: What the apparatus gathers — and where it stalls
scenes.character: Surveillance, fabrication, immobilisation, a public exhibit; the gods laugh; Hermes receives the deterrent as inducement. The scene stalls where the apparatus stalls.

entities.name: the goddesses — absent, shame unevenly distributed

text.kicker: #3 · the counterfeit gathering (C25); the Gestell comparison is the essay's own
text.title: The apparatus stalls at its own limit
text.italic: The net embodies capture organised as public evidence: it holds the relation visibly together while arresting the reciprocity through which it could move — and it cannot generate the trust needed to end the holding.

text.body: Helios makes the hidden encounter visible; Hephaestus converts knowledge into a worked arrangement of the chamber; Ares' own watch supplies the occasion. The capture succeeds — real grievance, real skill — yet what the held bodies become is a public exhibit to compel acknowledgment and repayment. The goddesses stay home; the male gods laugh at the ingenious capture; one draws the lesson

that the slow caught the swift. Apollo asks Hermes whether he would accept those bonds; Hermes would welcome three times as many, with all the gods looking on — the deterrent received as inducement. The laughter is no single moral verdict. Here the song stalls: exposure without payment, display without release, an account that cannot make Ares' future conduct present to inspection.

scenes.name: The word that takes on the debt
scenes.character: Poseidon's first promise is refused — a bad debtor makes a bad guarantee. He answers with his own payment; Hephaestus loosens the bonds with the same hands.

entities.name: Poseidon — the undertaking: he will pay if Ares fails
ἐγγύη — the surety itself, which no apparatus generates
Hephaestus — accepts what he cannot properly refuse; undoes his own work
the loosened bonds — released by the same craft

text.kicker: #4 · A23 trust under formal limit; A25 mediating office; C48
text.title: The word that takes on the debt
text.italic: Poseidon's undertaking proves-discloses trust beyond technical capture: a named participant's standing placed behind a continuation the present account cannot secure.

text.body: Poseidon promises Ares will pay; Hephaestus hears the weakness — the man who can depart can evade the payment. The answer is a changed undertaking: if Ares flees without paying, Poseidon will pay. This answers the objection without making Ares' future conduct present to inspection. Hephaestus judges it acceptable and uses his skill to undo his work; the same hands which assembled the constraint open it.

Occurrences: Poseidon's first promise and its refusal (#0, #4); the self-answerable liability (#4); the loosening (#4); Ares to Thrace, Aphrodite to Cyprus and Paphos where the Graces bathe, anoint and clothe her (#0, #5→0); Odysseus and the Phaeacians pleased by the song (#0, #5→0).

scenes.name: The relation after release
scenes.character: The spectators' scene no longer contains them; the claim persists, the work has changed, the guarantor has undertaken a cost, the lovers have paths beyond the image.

entities.name: Thrace — Ares' path out of the song
Paphos — precinct, fragrant altar; the Graces bathe, anoint, clothe
the emptied exhibit — what the bonds achieved, held against what they did not

text.title: The relation after release
text.italic: The whole demonstrates the difference between what the bonds achieved, what the undertaking enabled, and what the continuing field has still to bear.

text.body: Aphrodite reaches Paphos, where the Graces bathe, anoint and clothe her; Ares reaches Thrace; the hearers are pleased. Payment is not narrated; no child completes the release — Harmonia's genealogy and the Eros variants stand beside the ending, not inside it.
